title: Phát âm — Pronunciation primer: vowels and tones

segments.script: [EN: Welcome to Nghe Di. Before the lessons, a short guide to the sounds. We will group the vowels by the shape of your mouth.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [EN: Group one is rounded. Round your lips. Listen.] [VI_F: u] [EN: like the oo in food.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: ô] [EN: like the o in go.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: o] [EN: like the aw in saw.] [EN: Round your lips and repeat.] [PAUSE 4s] [VI: u] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI: ô] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI: o] [EN: Good.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [EN: Group two is neutral. Keep your lips relaxed, not rounded. This group is the hard one for English speakers.] [VI_F: ư] [EN: It is like the oo in food, but with your lips relaxed, not rounded.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: ơ] [EN: like the u in fur.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: â] [EN: the same sound, but short.] [EN: Relax your lips and repeat.] [PAUSE 4s] [VI: ư] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI: ơ] [EN: Good.]

[EN: Group three is smiling. Spread your lips into a smile, tongue forward. Listen.] [VI_F: i] [EN: like the ee in see.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: ê] [EN: like the ay in say.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: e] [EN: like the e in bed.] [EN: Smile and repeat.] [PAUSE 4s] [VI: i] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI: ê] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI: e] [EN: Good. Three mouth shapes — rounded, relaxed, and smiling.]

[EN: Now the contrast that matters most: rounded versus relaxed. Round your lips —] [VI_F: u] [EN: now relax them —] [VI_F: ư] [EN: Again. Rounded —] [VI_F: u] [EN: relaxed —] [VI_F: ư] [EN: You try. Rounded —] [PAUSE 3s] [VI: u] [EN: relaxed —] [PAUSE 3s] [VI: ư] [PAUSE 0.5s] [EN: One more pair, in real words.] [VI_F: cô] [EN: means aunt, with rounded lips.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: cơ] [EN: relaxed lips. Repeat the pair.] [PAUSE 4s] [VI: cô] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI: cơ] [EN: If you can hear and make that difference, the rest will come.]

[EN: Now the tones. In the south you will hear five. The same sound, a different pitch, a different meaning. Listen to one sound through all five.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: ma] [EN: a flat tone.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: mà] [EN: a falling tone.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: má] [EN: a high, rising tone.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: mả] [EN: a dipping tone. It falls, then rises.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [VI_F: mạ] [EN: a low tone, cut off short.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [EN: The writing has one more mark, but in the south it sounds the same as that dipping tone. Listen.] [VI_F: mã] [EN: The same sound.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [EN: Now you. A flat tone —] [PAUSE 3s] [VI: ma] [EN: a falling tone —] [PAUSE 3s] [VI: mà] [EN: a high, rising tone —] [PAUSE 3s] [VI: má] [EN: a dipping tone —] [PAUSE 3s] [VI: mả] [EN: Good. From the next lesson on, when a word's tone matters, I will describe it just like this — flat, falling, high and rising, dipping, or low and cut off short.]

[EN: That is enough to begin. Remember three mouth shapes — rounded, relaxed, and smiling — and five tones. Do not aim for perfection now; your ear will sharpen with every lesson.] [PAUSE 0.5s] [EN: Let us start. Lesson one is greetings.] [VI_F: Xin chào!]
